title: Accounts Assistant
description:
We are looking for an organised, detail-oriented Accounts Assistant to join our warm and welcoming finance team on a temporary basis for approximately 3 months, starting ASAP. Based on-site at our beautiful location near Cambridge, you will play a key role in keeping our day-to-day financial operations running smoothly.

Key Responsibilities
- Accounts Payable & Receivable: Effectively manage and deliver the AP and AR functions, ensuring all invoices, payments, and receipts are processed accurately, efficiently, and in compliance with company policies and procedures.
- Transaction Management: Ensure all financial transactions are complete, accurate, and thoroughly supported with clear documentation.
- Cross-Team Collaboration: Work closely with the Management Accountant, Assistant Management Accountant, and Commercial Finance Business Partners to support month-end processes and enable high-quality financial reporting.
- Query Resolution: Handle supplier and customer account queries promptly and professionally.

About You
- Previous experience working in an Accounts Assistant, Purchase/Sales Ledger, or finance administration role.
- High level of accuracy and strong attention to detail when processing financial data.
- Confident using accounting software and Microsoft Excel.
- Proactive, dependable, and comfortable working collaboratively in a friendly, office-based team.
- Available to start immediately (or at very short notice) and commit to a 3-month on-site assignment near Cambridge.

What We Offer
- The opportunity to work in a stunning, picturesque setting just outside Cambridge.
- A supportive, approachable, and very friendly team environment.
- Immediate start with hands-on exposure across both transactional finance and management reporting.

title: Accounts Assistant
description:

title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Accounts Assistant (Accounts Payable & Receivable)

Location: Cambridge (Outskirts)
Rate : £15.85 per hour
Job Type: Full-Time (37 hours per week)

About the Opportunity

A well-established and innovative organisation is seeking an Accounts Assistant to join its finance team. This is an excellent opportunity for someone looking to develop their career in finance while gaining exposure to a broad range of accounting responsibilities within a supportive and collaborative environment.

Working closely with finance colleagues, you will play a key role in ensuring the smooth operation of the Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable functions, maintaining accurate financial records, and supporting the delivery of high-quality financial reporting.

Key Responsibilities

Accounts Payable
- Process supplier invoices accurately and in a timely manner.
- Ensure invoices are appropriately authorised and correctly coded.
- Prepare and process payment runs.
- Resolve supplier queries and maintain positive working relationships.
- Monitor creditor balances and outstanding liabilities.

Accounts Receivable
- Raise customer invoices accurately and on time.
- Maintain the sales ledger and ensure data accuracy.
- Support credit control activities and monitor debtor balances.
- Investigate and resolve customer account queries.
- Allocate receipts and reconcile customer accounts.

Reconciliations & Finance Support
- Perform supplier, customer and bank reconciliations.
- Investigate and resolve discrepancies.
- Support month-end activities, including ledger reviews and accrual/prepayment processes.
- Assist with audit preparation and maintaining accurate financial records.

Stakeholder Engagement
- Act as a first point of contact for supplier and customer finance queries.
- Provide professional and timely support to internal and external stakeholders.
- Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives within the finance function.

Person Specification

Essential
- AAT qualified or currently studying towards AAT.
- Experience within Accounts Payable and/or Accounts Receivable.
- Experience working within a structured finance environment.
- Strong attention to detail and high levels of accuracy.
- Good organisational and time management skills.
- Strong Excel and data-handling capabilities.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Desirable
- Experience using Sage or a similar accounting system.
- Additional finance or accounting qualifications.

What's on Offer?
- Stable permanent opportunity within a growing organisation.
- Opportunity to support management accounting processes and develop broader finance skills.
- Collaborative and supportive team environment.
- Ongoing professional development opportunities.

title: Italian speaking Credit Controller
description:
Italian Speaking Credit Controller
- Location: Cambridge (Hybrid - 1 day per week in the office, 4 days remote)
- Salary: 35,000 - 38,000 + Excellent Benefits
- Languages: Fluent Italian and English required

The Opportunity

Our client is a globally recognised market leader with operations across Europe and international markets. Due to continued growth, they are seeking an Italian Speaking Credit Controller to join their established finance team and take responsibility for managing accounts receivable activities across the Italian market.

This is an excellent opportunity for a finance professional with credit control or accounts receivable experience to join a highly respected international organisation offering outstanding benefits, long-term career development and exceptional hybrid working flexibility.

The Role

As an Italian Speaking Credit Controller, you will be responsible for managing a portfolio of Italian customer accounts, ensuring timely collection of outstanding payments, reducing aged debt and maintaining strong customer relationships.

Working closely with Sales, Customer Service and Finance teams, you will play a key role in supporting healthy cash flow while delivering a professional and customer-focused service.

Key Responsibilities
- Manage a portfolio of Italian customer accounts and proactively collect outstanding invoices.
- Contact customers regarding overdue balances and negotiate payment solutions where required.
- Monitor credit exposure and recommend appropriate credit limits and account actions.
- Accurately allocate incoming payments and maintain customer account records.
- Issue customer statements, payment reminders and collection correspondence.
- Investigate and resolve payment disputes, invoice queries and account discrepancies.
- Build and maintain positive customer relationships while ensuring collection targets are achieved.
- Review orders and identify potential credit-related risks.
- Support internal and external audit activities.
- Ensure all account information is maintained accurately and updated within company systems.

Candidate Profile

To be successful in this role, you will possess:
- Fluent Italian and English language skills, both written and spoken.
- Previous experience within Credit Control, Accounts Receivable or a similar finance function.
- Proven experience managing customer accounts and collecting outstanding debt.
- Strong communication and relationship-building skills.
- Excellent attention to detail and organisational abilities.
- Confidence working towards collection targets and financial KPIs.
- Strong problem-solving and dispute-resolution skills.
- The ability to prioritise workload and manage multiple deadlines effectively.
- Experience using SAP or a similar ERP system would be advantageous.
- Knowledge of electronic invoicing processes would be beneficial.
- A collaborative approach with the ability to work effectively across multiple departments.

Salary & Benefits

In addition to a salary of 35,000 - 38,000, the company offers an excellent benefits package including Private Medical Insurance, Company Pension Scheme, Leisure Travel Insurance,Volunteer Leave,Compassionate & Care Leave,Employee Wellbeing Programmes,Hybrid Working (4 days working from home each week),Additional lifestyle and employee benefits

Why Apply?

This is a fantastic opportunity to join a highly successful international business where you can utilise your Italian language skills in a varied and rewarding finance role while benefiting from exceptional flexibility and a supportive working environment.

Apply Now

If you are an experienced Credit Controller or Accounts Receivable professional fluent in Italian and English, we'd love to hear from you.

Please send your CV to:

Jonathan Grimes
The Language Business

title: Logistics Coordinator
description:
Role: Logistics Coordinator

Location: Cambridge

Salary: 30,000 - 32,000

Hours: 08:00am - 16:30pm

Proactive are currently in search or an experienced Logistics Coordinator to start work in Cambridge. This is a permanent position and an exciting opportunity working for a market leading manufacturing company offering ample opportunity for progression and development.

You will be responsible for coordinating all aspects of logistics to ensure spare parts and machines are delivered to meet the business needs and to the latest customs regulations.

Principal Responsibilities:
- Coordinate all aspects of logistics operations while ensuring adherence to all relevant customs regulations.
- Coordinate the packing and dispatch of regular consolidation shipments to the central spares hub in Europe.
- Ensuring full accuracy of inventory, compliance with shipping documentation requirements, and adherence to delivery schedules.
- Manage and process all import clearances with third parties, ensuring accuracy and timely completion of all required documentation.
- Arrange all aspects of Spares, Freight, and Machine shipments, ensuring the preparation and accuracy of all export documentation in line with customer requirements.
- Obtain, review, and manage Machine and Freight quotations to secure cost-effective and compliant transport solutions.
- Optimise logistics processes and identify improvements across LCL (Low Container Load), FCL (Full Container Load), DG (Dangerous Goods by air, road, and sea), and international freight movements.
- Update and maintain all Logistics procedures and work instructions.
- Maintain a high level of knowledge across HTS codes, packing regulations, and country-specific export requirements.
- Act as Logistics representative for internal meeting and provide updates on current on-going machine shipment status.
- Strong understanding of international trade, Customs compliance, and Incoterms.

Working with:
- External contacts - Freight agents, Courier account reps, Insurance brokers, Customs Departments
- CS Team members / Installations
- Commercial Team members
- Operations Team Members
- R&D Team members

Knowledge and Experience
- Experience with freight forwarding, booking shipments, and preparing import / export documentation.
- Knowledge of HTS/HS codes, Incoterms and export packing.
- Experience in shipping dangerous goods by road and / or air would be beneficial.
- IT skills, especially Excel and Word.
- Experience in moving large machinery by road, air and sea.

title: Receptionist

Receptionist

Contract: Full-time, permanent Office-based

Peasgood & Skeates, part of Daniel Robinson & Sons, is a long-established, family-owned independent funeral directors with a proud history of supporting families and communities across Essex, Cambridgeshire, Suffolk and the surrounding areas.

We are looking for an experienced and compassionate Receptionist to join our flagship Cambridge office.

This is a particularly important role. As the first point of contact for families visiting or calling us, you'll help create a welcoming, supportive environment while providing the administrative coordination that keeps the branch running smoothly.

It's much more than a traditional reception position. You'll need excellent organisational skills, emotional intelligence and the ability to remain calm and professional when dealing with sensitive situations.

What you'll be doing
- Welcoming bereaved families, visitors and members of the public with warmth, dignity and discretion.
- Handling telephone enquiries sensitively, including initial calls following a death.
- Arranging appointments, viewings and chapel of rest visits.
- Coordinating diaries and sharing information between families, Funeral Directors and external contacts.
- Liaising with clergy, celebrants, crematoria, cemeteries, doctors, coroners, florists and other suppliers.
- Preparing and maintaining funeral paperwork, records and correspondence accurately.
- Handling payments, invoices and account enquiries.
- Managing incoming and outgoing post, emails and general administration.
- Maintaining reception, meeting rooms and public areas to a high standard.
- Providing wider administrative and branch support when required.
- Handling confidential information responsibly and in line with GDPR and company procedures.
- Supporting local community activities, events and fundraising where needed.

What we're looking for

Essential:
- Proven experience in a receptionist or front-of-house role.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
- A warm, professional and empathetic telephone manner.
- The emotional intelligence to support people who may be distressed or grieving.
- Strong administration, organisation and attention to detail.
- The ability to remain calm and manage competing priorities
- Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office, and confidence learning new systems.
- Discretion, integrity and professionalism.
- A smart and professional appearance and manner.
- A flexible, helpful approach and a genuine commitment to excellent customer service.

Desirable:
- At least one year's experience in a funeral directors' reception or similar role.
- Previous experience within the funeral industry.
- Knowledge of Cambridge and the surrounding area.
- Experience liaising with funeral-related organisations and third parties.
- Experience in another client-facing role involving sensitive or emotionally challenging situations.
- A full UK driving licence.
- A role that makes a difference

This is an opportunity to make a genuine difference to families during some of the most difficult moments of their lives. You'll be joining a well-established family business where compassion, professionalism and the quality of service provided to the local community really matter.

The role can be emotionally demanding, and you may occasionally come into contact with the deceased. We therefore ask applicants to consider this carefully before applying.

Apply today

If you're an experienced receptionist who combines excellent organisational skills with compassion, discretion and genuine warmth, we'd love to hear from you.

Please apply with your CV and a short covering note explaining why this opportunity appeals to you.
